sections.title: New in V32: Network and Errors
items: Network contains Device Config and IP Address’ sub-tabs. Its last selected page is remembered for the current project session.
Press Errors beside Report Issue to see the five most recently detected active issues. The red badge shows the total active count; Show All Errors opens the full review page.

Select an error or affected record to reveal its field. The app checks duplicate/invalid IP addresses, duplicate fixture IDs, missing patch addresses or modes, invalid DMX ranges and unconfirmed address overlaps in the Master Patch.
Corrected errors disappear. The list is session-only, not a saved history, and does not include power, rack, capacity or export checks.

Console tables in Control and Device Config cap TX Protocol and VLAN at 80 px, show parameter numbers without a label and use Uni for universes. Long VLAN, Role, Mode and SW values shrink within their cells; the full value remains available as a tooltip.

sections.title: Recommended Workflow
items: Press the menu button to open Actions, then open Project Info and enter the project name, dates, production details, and logos.
Add each distro with + Distro. Set its name, type, supply, voltage, RCBO rating, Socapex count, and any Aux or additional outputs.
Build the Fixture Patch by adding fixtures from the library or importing CSV, Excel, XLSM, or MVR data.

Open the full-page Positions workspace from Home Position Summary or Fixture Patch to create positions and assign up to three colours. Position names and colours are shared with the patch, power calculations, labels, Control, Rack Layout, Device Config, and IP Address'.
Open Power Calculations and assign distros to supplies. Enter fixture IDs to link each way to Fixture Patch data, then check phase totals, RCBO warnings, Aux outlets, and the PDF preview.

Use Control to add consoles and NPUs, including roles, locations, parameters, protocols, IP addresses, DMX ports, and reference images. When NPUs exist, use the Consoles and NPU sub-tabs to switch between them, and choose Card View or Table View for the required workflow. Add switches, nodes, and other network-capable hardware through Rack Layout or IP Address'.
Open Rack Layout to create racks, set their U size and depth, and place project or library devices from the Front or Rear view. Use Side view to inspect device depths and cable clearance.
Open Network → Device Config to review the synchronized device tree, expand individual ports, and edit patch, IP, subnet, protocol, direction, VLAN, and notes data.
Open Network → IP Address’ to review interfaces, assign subnet and VLAN information, and add IP-only devices used by the project.
Review the Fan Outs tab generated from Power Calculations and export the required Fan Out paperwork.
Use Distro Labels to complete Front RCBO Labels, Rear Labels, and Table View, then preview and export the required label pages.
Review Revisions from the Actions menu or Home card, then download the Lampy project file so the editable project can be reopened later.

sections.title: Fixture Patch, GDTF, and MVR
items: The fixture library shows GDTF ✅ only when a repository file has a fully matched manufacturer, fixture type, mode, and channel count. GDTF ❌ means an exact match is not currently available.
Use Import to load CSV, Excel, XLSM, or MVR files. Imported comparison tabs highlight new, removed, and changed patch data before it is merged into the master patch.

Fixture Patch Export groups paper, orientation, DPI, zoom, column, and GDTF controls inside Formatting Options. PDF, Excel, and MVR actions, temporary PDF logo controls, and the hidden-column report remain directly accessible below it.
MVR export checks fixture IDs, DMX addresses, modes, duplicate ranges, and GDTF availability before building the file.
V14 imports supported MVR 1.5 and 1.6 patch data, including fixture positions, layers, classes, UUID metadata, and embedded GDTF filenames with or without the .gdtf extension.
MVR export uses standards-formatted UUIDs and DMX addresses, creates one layer per Lampy fixture position, and embeds the exact matched GDTF file and mode.

Use Add GDTF Files in Fixture Patch Export when a repository match is unavailable. Manual upload remains a fallback and produces a report for matches, revisions, duplicates, missing fixtures, errors, and oversized files.

sections.title: Control, Device Config, Rack Layout, and IP Address'
items: Consoles and NPUs added in Control appear automatically in Device Config and IP Address'. When at least one NPU exists, Control displays separate Consoles and NPU sub-tabs.
Control groups consoles and NPUs by project position. Consoles are ordered Master, Backup, unassigned, then by name; NPUs remain sorted by name.

Choose Card View for device summary cards or Table View for Device Config-style editing, expandable ports, keyboard navigation, copy and paste, selection, and vertical drag-fill. The last Control view is remembered by the browser.

Device names, locations, roles, modes, software, parameters, IP addresses, port settings, protocols, VLANs, and notes remain linked between Control, Device Config, Rack Layout, and IP Address'. Rack position, mounting face, and physical dimensions remain controlled by Rack Layout.
Device Config branches are collapsed by default. Expand a device to see its Ethernet, fibre, XLR-5 DMX, and supported secondary-interface records.
Use arrow keys, Enter, Shift+Enter, Tab, and Shift+Tab to move through Device Config. Copy, paste, select ranges, or drag the fill handle vertically through compatible cells.
Rack Layout provides Front, Side, and Rear views. Front and Rear are mounting faces; Side is a depth overview where existing devices can still be moved vertically.
New racks default to 700 mm deep. Rack Depth can be edited, but every device must retain at least 100 mm of space behind it for cabling.
Front- and rear-mounted devices may share a U only when their combined depths plus the 100 mm cable space fit inside the rack.
Use Simple view for names and device types, or Detailed view for the front and rear line images supplied by the device library.
Use Port Configuration on supported DMX Nodes to assign universes, directions, names, and project positions. Assigned position colours appear on mapped DMX sockets in Detailed Rack Layout views.
Use + Network Device in IP Address' for IP-only equipment. Add reference-library rack hardware from Rack Layout.
Global Subnet can automatically supply the subnet for new devices. Manually changing an interface subnet excludes it from later global updates until Apply to all Devices is used.
Each device can contain two IP addresses. Subnet and VLAN values are stored per interface, while the device name, location, and notes remain shared.
The VLAN reference shows VLAN 0 Untagged/MGMT, VLAN 1 sACN, VLAN 2 Art-Net, and VLAN 3 RoboCam with matching table colours.
A Notes value of SPARE uses the project-wide SPARE styling automatically.

sections.title: Power Calculations
items: Fixture IDs link Power Calculations to Fixture Patch names, watts, positions, and position colours. Duplicate fixture IDs are highlighted.

Use the arrow keys, Enter, Shift+Enter, Tab, and Shift+Tab to move between editable Power Calculations cells. Drag the selected cell's blue fill handle vertically to copy a value through a compatible column.
Choose Full Name or Short Name independently for the Power Calculations display.
Select a 16 Amp or 10 Amp RCBO in each distro's settings. A way is warned above 15.01 A for a 16 Amp RCBO or above 9.01 A for a 10 Amp RCBO.
Aux outlets are grouped in threes for Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3. Only Aux outlets enabled for power calculations contribute to the totals. Configured 3ø Outputs are shown separately.
Use Power Calcs for detailed assignments and Phase Totals for the supply and connected-distro overview.
The PDF preview keeps Socapex groups together, starts each distro on a new page, shows four Socapexes per page, and finishes with the supply phase-total summary.
Fan Outs use the Power Calculations assignments to produce display-only Socapex, fixture ID, fixture type, and position paperwork.

sections.title: Distro Labels
items: Front RCBO Labels, Rear Labels, and Table View edit the same distro data, so changes remain synchronized between views.
Table View supports spreadsheet-style keyboard navigation, shift-selection, copy and paste, and vertical drag-fill across editable Socapex, Aux, and Output cells.
Choose Full Name or Short Name in Table View to display the linked fixture-library name without changing manually entered fixture text.
Socapex, Aux, and Output labels support label formatting and colour controls. Socapex names and colours also appear in Power Calculations.
Choose Full Name or Short Name for Front RCBO Labels without changing the fixture's stored library name.
Use Label Settings and Label Format before opening Export. Select the required front and rear pages, paper size, orientation, and logos in the preview.

sections.title: Revisions and Saving
items: Changes to Project Info, Fixture Patch, Power Calculations, and Control automatically create concise revision notes in the latest working version.
Use Bump Version Number to increment the project version and add the current date. Notes can be edited, removed, or moved to another version.
Similar automatic changes are grouped into a short client-facing summary. Use Download Change Log when the detailed activity log is needed.
The browser saves a working copy locally, but Download Project is the portable backup. Use Open Project to continue from a saved Lampy project file.

sections.title: Useful Tips
items: The Home tab provides clickable totals for Fixtures, Universes, Consoles, parameters, Distros, Socapexes, and Data Racks. These open the relevant project page directly.

Use Customise Home to reorder, resize, hide, restore, or collapse dashboard cards. Changes are stored with the current project; Set as Browser Default applies the chosen layout to future and legacy projects.

Use Edit at the top of Position Summary to open the Positions workspace. Renaming a position updates linked fixtures and devices; removing one clears it from affected project records after confirmation.
Opening Universes from Home displays a full-page Universe Detail view with one tab per patched universe. Use Back to Home when finished.
Move the pointer over a main Sheet tab, or focus it with the keyboard, to display its available sub-tabs and project pages for faster navigation.
Fixture group title lines always use the full fixture name. Full Name and Short Name options affect supported table cells and labels only.
Use the Fixture Patch lock before editing rows, and watch for duplicate fixture IDs or overlapping DMX addresses. Show/Hide Columns is available beside Clear Filters in the Filter & Sort controls.
Supply cards can be collapsed after setup to keep Power Calculations tidy.
Project logos are controlled in Project Info and can be included in supported exports.
All project, GDTF, and MVR processing is local to the browser. Lampy Paperwork does not import grandMA3 .show files or modify grandMA3 system libraries.
Use Report Issue for bugs, missing fixture requests, or feature suggestions.
